market_holds: Spot $14.30 at the 2026-11-09 close (sealed baseline). The stock is up 18% from $12.07 on 11-03, after +8.4% on 11-04 and +11.6% on 11-06 (Yahoo daily bars). Those two days line up with Ouster's +15.7% (Q3 print on 11-03 after the close) and +14% days, so the run-up reads as lidar-sector sympathy, not Hesai news; AAII on 11-09 names no catalyst. Before that the stock fell about 25% from ~$16 (10-09) to $12, including heavy-volume drops on 10-21/22 around a broker preview, and it sits 50% below its 52-week high. Options: front-expiry event-implied move 6.5%, 25-delta skew -3.6 vol points (calls bid), put/call OI 0.72, so the options lean upside. Consensus: Earnings Whispers $159.53M Q3 revenue (about RMB1.08bn at the guide's FX), below the RMB1.10-1.15bn guide; other aggregators show $165.1M (Benzinga/EW snippet) and RMB1.166bn (Chartmill), so the consensus has been cut but not cleanly. One broker note of 2026-10-22 expects RMB1.05bn, below guide, on softer ADAS demand and weaker lawn-mower orders; it cut its 2026E revenue to RMB3.72bn, implying a Q4 near RMB1.13bn, about flat on Q3. FY2026 lidar target 3.0-3.5M units with ~1.1M shipped in H1. Last four results reactions were all negative: Mar-2026 about -8.8%, May-19 -9.0%, Aug-18 gap -12.8% / close -5.3% (Q3 guide below the street's $176.5M). Bullish sentiment is low (EW: 12.1%).
view: The Hesai-specific evidence points to a soft print. Q2 landed at the bottom of its guide (RMB860.8M vs 850-900M) with blended ASP down 35% year on year. Q3 has to step up 28-34% sequentially on 800-850k units. Gasgoo's installation counts put Hesai's China passenger-vehicle lidar installs at about 228k in July and only about 127k in August. RoboSense's Q3 ADAS units jumped to 450k (+200% YoY) and Huawei retook the cumulative lead, so Hesai is losing share at the margin. Li Auto, a core multi-lidar customer, is shrinking (October 29k, -8.6% YoY). One broker has published a below-guide Q3. The FY 3.0-3.5M unit target needs a Q4 of about 1.1M+ units, which looks hard against that broker's flat-Q4 revenue. So the likely shape is a Q3 at or slightly below the low end and a Q4 guide that does not support the FY target: the same pattern that produced four straight down reactions. Most of the Q3 shortfall is already in the price: the October selloff and a consensus cut below the guide low. What is not is the last week. The stock has rallied 18% on Ouster's results and robotics/physical-AI enthusiasm, which Hesai's China ADAS numbers do not validate, and the options pay for upside into the print. Against that, management reliably leans on the physical-AI/SGI narrative (Kosmo first revenue, actuation modules, Mercedes L3, VW China wins), and that is the same story the sector rally is buying. A seasonal Q4 guide could clear a cautious bar, and sentiment is depressed. Net: a modest down lean, not strong enough to recommend.
unpriced: The 18% sector-sympathy run-up of 11-04 to 11-06, tied to Ouster and not to any Hesai datapoint, has partly reversed the October de-rating. The price now holds more optimism than the company-specific evidence supports (China ADAS share and ASP pressure, a published below-guide Q3, FY unit target at risk), so a merely in-line-with-cut-consensus print has room to give the bounce back. Not strong enough to act on, because the deciding line (the Q4 guide) is unobservable before the release.

recommendation.reason: The evidence leans down: a published below-guide Q3, share loss to RoboSense/Huawei in installation data, ASP compression, a weak Li Auto, and a sympathy rally that front-ran the print. But consensus has already been cut below the guide low, and the line the stock trades on (the Q4 guide and the FY unit target) cannot be seen before the release. Confidence is below the playbook's 65 bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue guide clearly above ~RMB1.2bn, with the FY 3.0-3.5M unit target reaffirmed, or a step-up in SGI revenue toward the RMB200-300M FY guide, would validate the sector rally and send the stock up.

self_critique: Consensus already sits below the guide low and October priced a miss, so a RMB1.05-1.10bn Q3 may be a non-event. Hesai's Q4 is seasonally strongest, and management may guide a big Q4 or keep the FY unit target. Its physical-AI story (Kosmo revenue, actuators, Mercedes/VW wins) is exactly what the sector is rewarding right now, and low sentiment plus call-skew demand could fuel a squeeze. Four straight negative reactions are the kind of pattern the market itself may now be over-discounting. The August install figure is derived from two cumulative tables and could reflect reporting noise.
approach_notes: P4 (prove priced-in) helped: the consensus had visibly moved below the guide, which kept me from shorting a known miss. P3's physical series (Gasgoo cumulative installs) was useful but one month stale. Comparing peer tapes (OUST) to explain the run-up was the most useful step and is not named in the playbook.
